label: John 18:1
text: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went out with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered.

label: John 18:2
text: Now Judas, who betrayed him, also knew the place, for Jesus often met there with his disciples.

label: John 18:3
text: Judas then, having taken a detachment of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.

label: John 18:4
text:
Jesus therefore, knowing all the things that were happening to him, went out, and said to them,
“Who are you looking for?”

label: John 18:5
text:
They answered him, “Jesus of Nazareth.”
Jesus said to them,
“I am he.”
Judas also, who betrayed him, was standing with them.

variants.reading: ο παραδιδους αυτον ('the one betraying him') omitted
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 18:5): the phrase 'ο παραδιδους αυτον' (the one betraying him, i.e. 'Judas also, who betrayed him, was standing with them') is omitted in P66* and syr s; the WEB prints it. P66 is a manuscript node of this graph.

label: John 18:6
text:
When therefore he said to them,
“I am he,” they went backward, and fell to the ground.

label: John 18:7
text:
Again therefore he asked them,
“Who are you looking for?”
They said, “Jesus of Nazareth.”

label: John 18:8
text:
Jesus answered,
“I told you that I am he. If therefore you seek me, let these go their way,”

label: John 18:9
text:
that the word might be fulfilled which he spoke,
“Of those whom you have given me, I have lost none.”

label: John 18:10
text: Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it, and struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.

label: John 18:11
text:
Jesus therefore said to Peter,
“Put the sword into its sheath. The cup which the Father has given me, shall I not surely drink it?”

variants.reading: παντες γαρ οι λαβοντες μαχαιραν εν μαχαιρα απολουνται ('for all who take the sword will perish by the sword') added
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 18:11): the Matthean-sounding sentence is an addition in Codex Koridethi (Theta) only; none of the graph's manuscript nodes carries it, so attested_by is empty. The seed lead's report that John 18:11 is absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus is not borne out by the fetched articles (see notes.md).

label: John 18:12
text: So the detachment, the commanding officer, and the officers of the Jews, seized Jesus and bound him,

label: John 18:13
text: and led him to Annas first, for he was father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.

label: John 18:14
text: Now it was Caiaphas who advised the Jews that it was expedient that one man should perish for the people.

label: John 18:15
text: Simon Peter followed Jesus, as did another disciple. Now that disciple was known to the high priest, and entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest;

label: John 18:16
text: but Peter was standing at the door outside. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to her who kept the door, and brought in Peter.

label: John 18:17
text:
Then the maid who kept the door said to Peter, “Are you also one of this man’s disciples?”
He said, “I am not.”

label: John 18:18
text: Now the servants and the officers were standing there, having made a fire of coals, for it was cold. They were warming themselves. Peter was with them, standing and warming himself.

label: John 18:19
text: The high priest therefore asked Jesus about his disciples, and about his teaching.

label: John 18:20
text:
Jesus answered him,
“I spoke openly to the world. I always taught in synagogues, and in the temple, where the Jews always meet. I said nothing in secret.

label: John 18:21
text: Why do you ask me? Ask those who have heard me what I said to them. Behold, these know the things which I said.”

variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 18:21): επερωτας ('interrogate') in D, syr s, f1, f13 and Byz 2 against ερωτας ('ask'), read by Sinaiticus*, A, B, C, L, W, Theta, Psi, 054, 0250, 33, 1424; the WEB follows 'ask'. None of the graph's manuscript nodes carries the επερωτας reading.

label: John 18:22
text: When he had said this, one of the officers standing by slapped Jesus with his hand, saying, “Do you answer the high priest like that?”

label: John 18:23
text:
Jesus answered him,
“If I have spoken evil, testify of the evil; but if well, why do you beat me?”

label: John 18:24
text: Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas, the high priest.

label: John 18:25
text:
Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said therefore to him, “You aren’t also one of his disciples, are you?”
He denied it, and said, “I am not.”

label: John 18:26
text: One of the servants of the high priest, being a relative of him whose ear Peter had cut off, said, “Didn’t I see you in the garden with him?”

label: John 18:27
text: Peter therefore denied it again, and immediately the rooster crowed.

label: John 18:28
text: They led Jesus therefore from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. It was early, and they themselves didn’t enter into the Praetorium, that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.

label: John 18:29
text: Pilate therefore went out to them, and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”

label: John 18:30
text: They answered him, “If this man weren’t an evildoer, we wouldn’t have delivered him up to you.”

label: John 18:31
text:
Pilate therefore said to them, “Take him yourselves, and judge him according to your law.”
Therefore the Jews said to him, “It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death,”

label: John 18:32
text: that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spoke, signifying by what kind of death he should die.

label: John 18:33
text: Pilate therefore entered again into the Praetorium, called Jesus, and said to him, “Are you the King of the Jews?”

label: John 18:34
text:
Jesus answered him,
“Do you say this by yourself, or did others tell you about me?”

label: John 18:35
text: Pilate answered, “I’m not a Jew, am I? Your own nation and the chief priests delivered you to me. What have you done?”

label: John 18:36
text:
Jesus answered,
“My Kingdom is not of this world. If my Kingdom were of this world, then my servants would fight, that I wouldn’t be delivered to the Jews. But now my Kingdom is not from here.”

label: John 18:37
text:
Pilate therefore said to him, “Are you a king then?”
Jesus answered,
“You say that I am a king. For this reason I have been born, and for this reason I have come into the world, that I should testify to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice.”

label: John 18:38
text:
Pilate said to him, “What is truth?”
When he had said this, he went out again to the Jews, and said to them, “I find no basis for a charge against him.

label: John 18:39
text: But you have a custom, that I should release someone to you at the Passover. Therefore, do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”

label: John 18:40
text: Then they all shouted again, saying, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a robber.

label: Jesus crossed the Kidron with his disciples to a garden
statement: Jesus went out with his disciples across the brook Kidron to a garden on its far side, which they entered.

label: Jesus often met his disciples in the garden; Judas knew the place
statement: Jesus often met his disciples at that garden, so Judas knew the place.

label: Judas came with a detachment of soldiers and Jewish officers
statement: Judas brought a speira (detachment) of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, with lanterns, torches and weapons, to the garden.

label: A Roman cohort was stationed in Jerusalem at the Antonia Fortress
statement: The detachment (speira) was the Roman cohort stationed in Jerusalem, quartered in the Antonia Fortress adjoining the Temple.

label: Peter cut off the right ear of Malchus, the high priest's servant
statement: Simon Peter drew a sword and cut off the right ear of Malchus, the servant of the high priest; John alone gives the servant's name and the 'right' ear.

label: The detachment was commanded by a chiliarchos (commanding officer)
statement: The arresting detachment was commanded by a chiliarchos ('commanding officer', literally commander of a thousand), who with the officers of the Jews seized and bound Jesus.

label: Jesus was taken first to Annas, then sent to Caiaphas
statement: Jesus was led first to Annas and questioned there, and then sent bound by Annas to Caiaphas the high priest.

label: Annas had been high priest; his family kept control of the office
statement: Annas son of Seth had been high priest (AD 6-15) and remained head of the family that dominated the high priesthood; five of his sons later held the office.

label: Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas
statement: John states that Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.

label: An unnamed disciple known to the high priest brought Peter in
statement: Another disciple, unnamed, was known to the high priest, entered the high priest's court with Jesus, and brought Peter in at the door.

label: Peter denied three times in the courtyard; the rooster crowed
statement: Peter denied three times in the high priest's courtyard, while warming himself at a fire, and after the third denial the rooster crowed.

label: A charcoal fire in the courtyard, for it was cold
statement: The servants and officers had made a fire of coals (anthrakia) in the courtyard, for it was cold, and were warming themselves; Peter stood with them.

label: The high priest questioned Jesus; an officer slapped him
statement: The high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching, and an officer slapped him for his answer.

label: The leaders stayed outside to avoid defilement and eat the Passover
statement: The Judean leaders would not enter the Praetorium, to avoid ritual defilement, so that they could eat the Passover; in John's chronology the Passover meal falls on the evening after the trial.

label: It was not lawful for the Jews to put anyone to death
statement: The Judean leaders told Pilate it was not lawful for them to put anyone to death, so the death sentence had to come from the Roman governor.

label: Pilate questioned Jesus about being King of the Jews
statement: Pilate questioned Jesus about the charge 'King of the Jews', the political title on which the governor could act.

label: The crowd chose Barabbas; John calls him a robber
statement: The crowd shouted for Barabbas rather than Jesus; John alone characterizes Barabbas as a robber (lestes).
